models.name: Predator 57 Mk II
models.referenceConfiguration: Predator 57 Mk II with hardtop, three guest cabins for six, full-beam owner suite, lower saloon, tender garage and single crew cabin; engine choice and owner finishes are recorded as options rather than modeled as separate generations.

facts.label: Generation boundary
facts.value: Mk II production 2017–2019; predecessor Mk I 2015–2017
facts.note: Independent model-history tracking separates two generations and dates the Mk II production window.

facts.label: Length overall
facts.note: YachtBuyer principal characteristics list 59 ft 10 in / 18.24 m.

facts.label: Beam
facts.note: Independent delivered-vessel listing reports 4.70 m beam for the Mk II.

facts.label: Draft
facts.note: Independent delivered-vessel listing reports 1.30 m draft.

facts.label: Fuel capacity
facts.note: The principal characteristics give 581 US gallons, represented here as the rounded 2,200 L catalogue value.

facts.label: Fresh-water capacity
facts.note: The principal characteristics give 158 US gallons, represented here as the rounded 600 L catalogue value.

facts.label: Black-water capacity
facts.note: The principal characteristics give 39 US gallons, represented here as the rounded 150 L catalogue value.

facts.label: Guest accommodation
facts.value: 6 guests in 3 cabins; full-beam master, double cabin and twin/bunk cabin
facts.note: The independent specification identifies three cabins and six guests with the stated berth arrangement.

facts.label: Guest and day heads
facts.value: 2 guest heads plus 1 shared day head
facts.note: The independent accommodation section lists two guest heads and one shared day head.

facts.label: Engine options
facts.value: Twin Volvo Penta D13-800, D13-900 or D11 IPS950
facts.note: The manufacturer options reproduced by YachtBuyer show the three available twin-engine configurations.

facts.label: Maximum speed
facts.note: The Mk II principal characteristics quote 33 knots; the page also notes up to 40 knots depending on selected option, so the catalog keeps the principal value and records the conflict as an uncertainty.

facts.label: Maximum range
facts.note: YachtBuyer lists a 325 nm maximum range for the reference configuration.

facts.label: Hull and superstructure
facts.note: The principal characteristics identify GRP for both hull and superstructure.

layout.description: A two-level hardtop sports yacht with an opening roof and saloon opening to the cockpit. The reference arrangement uses three guest cabins, a full-beam amidships owner suite, two guest heads, a shared day head and a separate single crew cabin.

visual.hullDescription: GRP deep-V planing hull with a long sportscruiser sheer and broad aft platform.
visual.superstructureDescription: Low hardtop sportsboat profile with opening roof, lowering patio door and a compact tender-garage transom.
visual.glazingDescription: Oversized pillarless side glazing and restyled saloon windows are the Mk II visual cue, paired with a forward windscreen and opening roof.

uncertainties: YachtBuyer presents a headline capability of up to 40 knots depending on option while its principal characteristics give 33 knots; the catalog uses 33 knots for the reference configuration.
Exact production quantity and factory completion dates are not published; the 2017–2019 boundary is independent model-history evidence.
Owner-specific four-cabin and engine layouts are excluded from the modeled reference configuration.

models.name: Manhattan 63
models.referenceConfiguration: Manhattan 63 flybridge motor yacht with four guest cabins for up to eight, main-deck saloon, aft galley, flybridge helm and separate crew/service spaces; optional owner layouts excluded.

facts.label: Production window
facts.note: Independent model timeline dates development and production from 2010 through 2015.

facts.label: Length overall
facts.note: YachtBuyer lists 21.07 m / 69 ft 2 in LOA.

facts.label: Beam
facts.note: Independent comparison lists 5.13 m maximum beam.

facts.label: Draft at full load
facts.note: Independent comparison lists 1.60 m full-load draft.

facts.label: Guest accommodation
facts.note: YachtBuyer identifies up to eight guests and four cabins.

facts.label: Maximum speed
facts.note: Independent model overview quotes 33 knots maximum speed.

facts.label: Cruising speed
facts.note: Independent overview describes a comfortable 22-knot cruise with MAN V8-1000 engines.

facts.label: Standard range
facts.note: Independent overview quotes 809 nm standard range.

facts.label: Hull material
facts.note: The model is described as a GRP flybridge yacht.

facts.label: Model award
facts.value: Motor Boat Awards 2012, Flybridge over 55 ft
facts.note: YachtBuyer records the 2012 Flybridge over 55 ft award.

sources.title: Sunseeker Manhattan 63 yachts for sale and model overview

sources.title: Sunseeker previous-model archive
sources.scope: Manufacturer archive context for the Manhattan heritage range.

layout.description: Three logical levels comprise the open flybridge, main-deck saloon/galley and lower guest accommodation. The standard reference arrangement is four guest cabins for up to eight with a separate crew/service zone.

visual.hullDescription: Long GRP planing flybridge hull with broad aft quarters and a high-volume cruising form.
visual.superstructureDescription: Raised main-deck saloon with a full flybridge, aft dining zone and forward helm arrangement typical of the Manhattan family.
visual.glazingDescription: Panoramic main-deck saloon glazing and large lower-deck hull windows emphasize the light-filled four-cabin interior.

uncertainties: Exact engine option and tank capacities were not consistently exposed in the independent pages used for this batch and remain null rather than inferred.
YachtBuyer reports development beginning in 2010 and first production later that year; no factory build ledger was located.
Owner-specific cabin and crew layouts are excluded from the reference configuration.
